title: Pre-Analysis — Retention of the Photoluminescent Escape Path Marking as a Spares Option
abstract: Closed pre-analysis of a lessor-driven proposal to keep the photoluminescent escape path marking available as a low-cost spares option for the early fleet. The proposal was not sustained.

sections.objective: Two lessors with early aircraft coming off lease asked whether the photoluminescent marking strip could be kept available as a spares option, so that damaged runs could be repaired in kind rather than triggering a conversion to the diode standard at redelivery. The order had to establish whether that is a supportable configuration position or simply a cheaper one, and what it would do to the emergency lighting compliance statement on those aircraft.
sections.findings_summary: Five items were confirmed and the first is decisive. The diode standard supersedes the photoluminescent strip rather than sitting alongside it, and the supersession is written into the compliance statement: an aircraft is compliant through one means or the other and the means is recorded per aircraft. Keeping the strip available does not preserve a second compliant configuration, it preserves a repair route for aircraft whose recorded means of compliance is already migrating. The installation bulletin for the diode standard is open on all the aircraft concerned. The parts content, the installation task and the cabin divider lining work that shares the same sidewall junction all treat the strip as a superseded item. None of that is a reason to keep it, and the cost argument does not survive the compliance one.
sections.next_steps: Decline the proposal and confirm to both lessors that damaged photoluminescent runs at redelivery trigger the diode conversion for that section, not a like-for-like repair. Ask spares to hold a defined residual stock against in-service damage only, with an end date tied to the last aircraft converted, and record that as a support decision rather than a configuration one. Add the note limiting the strip bonding procedure to damage repair before conversion, so the maintenance manual does not keep suggesting a route the compliance statement no longer supports. Close the order.

similarity_seeds: recorded means of compliance for emergency escape path marking
like for like repair of a superseded cabin item at lease redelivery

tasks.title: Establish the recorded means of compliance per aircraft
Traverse the marking supersession chain and open bulletins
Size a residual spares holding against in-service damage only

expected_findings.rationale: The diode standard supersedes the strip and the compliance statement records one means per aircraft. Keeping the strip orderable does not preserve a second compliant configuration; it only preserves a repair route for a configuration that is already being withdrawn.
expected_findings.resolution: Decline the proposal and state the single means of compliance per aircraft in the reply to both lessors.

expected_findings.rationale: The diode installation bulletin is open on every aircraft named in the proposal. Retaining a like-for-like repair route in parallel would leave two live routes to two different recorded configurations on the same aircraft.
expected_findings.resolution: Keep the bulletin as the only route and set the residual spares holding against in-service damage before conversion only.

expected_findings.rationale: The strip is already marked as superseded in the figure. Reinstating it as an orderable option would mean reversing a supersession in the parts content, which the technical publications process has no route for.
expected_findings.resolution: No action. The absence of a reversal route is itself part of the answer to the lessors.

expected_findings.rationale: The installation task still carries the strip bonding procedure under a pre-modification effectivity, which is what made the proposal look feasible in the first place. It is retained for in-service damage repair, not for redelivery conversion, and does not say so.
expected_findings.resolution: Add a note limiting the strip procedure to damage repair before conversion.

expected_findings.rationale: The forward divider bay lining candidate disturbs the same sidewall to floor junction where the marking run terminates. Whichever marking standard is fitted, that termination has to be remade, which weakens the like-for-like repair argument further.
expected_findings.resolution: Note the termination rework in the lining candidate scope so it is costed once.

expected_non_findings.reason: Shares cabin floor zone 241 and the ATA 25-20 chapter and reads as forward cabin floor work in the same region, but it is a corrosion-driven seat track substructure change with no lighting or marking content and no shared part number or functional item.

type_data.conclusion: Closed and rejected. The compliance position rather than the cost position decided it: the strip is a withdrawn means of compliance, not a cheaper alternative one.
